oewn-10409097-n.learner: A person who has something that belongs to them.
examples: It was impossible for her to see the word without thinking of Pemberley and its owner.
All her apprehension of meeting its owner returned.

oewn-10408623-n.learner: A person who, by law, is the one a business belongs to.
examples: She is the owner of a small bakery in town.

oewn-02647119-v.learner: To stop doing something for a short time and then go on with it.
examples: After pausing on this point a considerable while, she once more continued to read.
Miss Bennet paused a little, and then replied.

oewn-00781106-v.learner: To stop an action for a short time.
examples: Let's pause here for a short break.

oewn-00079838-n.learner: The act of getting something by paying money for it.
examples: I should think it more possible to get Pemberley by purchase than by imitation.

oewn-13274511-n.learner: A thing that someone has bought.
examples: She showed us her latest purchase, a blue coat.

oewn-11435456-n.learner: Something that gives you a way to have influence or to gain an advantage.
examples: The new facts gave the lawyers little purchase on the case.

oewn-11493538-n.learner: The extra force you get when you are in a position to use a lever.
examples: He pushed the bar further under the rock to get more purchase.

oewn-04890163-n.learner: Control over yourself in what you do on your own and with other people.
examples: He showed great restraint and did not shout back.

oewn-06257831-n.learner: A rule or condition that limits how free you are.
examples: The new law put restraints on how much the banks could lend.

oewn-01147872-n.learner: The act of controlling someone or something by holding them back.
examples: The small shops suffered from the restraint of trade by the big companies.

oewn-14022266-n.learner: The state of being held so that you cannot move freely.
examples: The prisoner was kept under restraint.

oewn-04704790-n.learner: The quality of having little or no decoration.
examples: The room was decorated with great restraint, with plain white walls.

oewn-04088956-n.learner: A device that slows down or holds back the movement of something.
examples: The child was held in the seat by a safety restraint.

oewn-05106204-n.learner: How big or small something is.
examples: You ought to make some kind of remark on the size of the room, or the number of couples.
He went pale when he saw the size of the bill.
It is the only town of any size in that area.

oewn-05102953-n.learner: Which one of a set of fixed, graded measures something is, as with clothes.
examples: She wears a size 8 dress.
He lost his job, and that's about the size of it.

oewn-14730533-n.learner: Any sticky substance used to fill the tiny holes in a surface or to make cloth stiff.
examples: The painter brushed size onto the wall before hanging the paper.

oewn-07244190-n.learner: Talk in which you describe yourself as the best, the greatest, or the most.
examples: It is often only carelessness of opinion, and sometimes an indirect boast.
Mr. Darcy's shameful boast of what misery he had been able to inflict gave her a keener sense of her sister's sufferings.

connotation.why: frames self-description as vain against a plain claim or statement

oewn-00736950-v.learner: To write a line on something giving its date, or simply to mark it with a date.
examples: It was dated from Rosings, at eight o'clock in the morning.
The latter half, which was dated a day later, gave more important intelligence.

oewn-00620873-v.learner: To give something a date, or to work out when it most likely happened or was made.
examples: I believe I must date it from my first seeing his beautiful grounds at Pemberley.

oewn-02491462-v.learner: To go out with someone on a planned romantic meeting.
examples: He dated her once, but they never met again.

oewn-02491850-v.learner: To go out with someone regularly and have a steady romantic relationship with them.
examples: They have been dating for two years.

oewn-00737394-v.learner: To press a stamp showing the date onto something.
examples: The clerk dated each form with a rubber stamp.

oewn-00306956-r.learner: A long way down or a long way in.
examples: They dug deep to find water.
The soldiers pushed deep into enemy land.

oewn-00307214-r.learner: Until a late point in time.
examples: They talked deep into the night.

oewn-02597468-v.learner: To do something even though you think it is beneath you.
examples: Mr. Wickham touched his hat--a salutation which Mr. Darcy just deigned to return.
Mrs. Bennet deigned not to make any reply.

connotation.why: casts the doer as acting from felt superiority, against plain agree or do

oewn-02004165-v.learner: To guide or lead someone to a place.
examples: Mr. Darcy handed the ladies into the carriage.
He then handed her in, Maria followed.

oewn-02235554-v.learner: To put something into someone's hands or into their care.
examples: Please hand me the spoon.
